plates.table: Book VI, the Normanni (Northmen) alphabet made from Greek numerals, which Trithemius reports on Bede's testimony - Wellcome copy
plates.layout: Three columns of eight: red Latin letter, black Greek numeral sign, red Arabic number.

letters.note: δ is cut as an S/ʃ-like hook
stigma cut like a 'ꞇ'/'ϛ' with a hooked top
ζ cut like a blackletter 3; red number 7 printed as an open 'ʌ'-like 7
θ cut with the bar run out on both sides
ιϛ looks like 'iq'
ιζ is cut as a joined ι+ζ, reading like 'Iʒ'
Trithemius says on this page that he added w as the 24th letter for German and formed it 'sic, κδ'

plates.letters_note: The 1000-sign is a hooked mark like a question mark without its dot (a reversed-c head on a short tail; cf. the abbreviation ꝯ); from 2000 on it follows a letter (b+sign = 2000 ...). Uses 'h' in the b-like form of the type; includes & (6), r rotunda (100), long s (200) and round s (300). This is NOT the scheme announced in the preface on 2p2v ('IOANNES TRITEMIVS ABBAS PEAPOLITANVS LECTORI S.', signed 'Scripsi xvi. Martij. Anno M.D.viij.', Wellcome _0488): that preface adds four doublets to the 24 letters - m and final m, r and the 2-shaped final r, long s and final s, closed v and open u - for the numbers of Book V, and does not mention &. The sentence above this table says so itself: 'Alius est autem iste modus numerandi ab eo quem in libro quinto posuimus'.

problems: Two copies disagree in two places: (1) Book V tabula recta, red foot row - Wellcome 'w a b c d a f', LoC 'w a b c d e f'; (2) Book VI transposition table (2q5r) - no cipher opposite 's' in the Wellcome copy, a hooked sign in the LoC copy. The specimen line below the transposition table prints the hooked sign for s in both copies, so the Wellcome blank is a dropped sort in the table, not a different key.

Doracus table (2q2r): 30 signs but 29 labels - the 6th sign of column 1 has no label in either copy; 'f' is printed half a line above its sign; column 3 has two 'm'-labelled and two 'n'-labelled signs as printed (m, n, n). Do not 'correct'.
Hichi table (2q3v): 'm' is printed twice (last of column 2, first of column 3), checked in both copies.
Tironian alphabet (2q6v): 'm' and 'n' each printed twice (column 3: k l m m n n), checked in both copies.
The roman type's h has a closed b-like bowl throughout (recta, numerals, pair table): read 'b' carefully; position decides.

Red was printed in a separate pass and is out of register; in tables with red signs (Wastbald, Doracus, Otfrid, Sequitur aliud, Hichi, Pharamund, Beda, Theban labels, alchemist, Tironian) a red fragment touching a black label belongs to the red sign, not to the label.

Labels are lower-case blackletter/rotunda in the sign tables and roman in the numeral tables and the transposition table (2q5r); the Normanni table of 2p6v prints capital-like 'A' and 'F'; 'v' is printed for u/v in the sign tables, while the tabula recta and the numeral-pair table print 'u'. j never occurs; w is always last; ʒ is the z.

The 2r2r-2r4v number tables ('Orchema numerale pro literis', 'Prima' and 'Secunda tabula expansionis anomale', the zodiac and planet number-alphabets) are NOT cropped: they are Latin letters paired with numbers under zodiac and planet signs, nothing to trace. notes: BOOK NUMBER SETTLED for 1518: the alphabet catalogue is in Book VI. Book V ends on 2p4v ('quintum quoque Polygraphiae librum terminamus. Anno d[omi]ni M.D.VIII.') and Book VI opens on 2p5r with the heading 'LIBER POLYGRAPHIAE SEXTVS INITIVM SVMIT' (Wellcome _0492 and _0493, read). The 1561 French prints the same matter under the running head 'LIVRE CINQVIESME'.

ORDER OF THE BOOK VI CATALOGUE (1518, Wellcome file index / signature): Normanni from Greek numerals (_0496, 2p6v); Wastbald (_0498, 2q1v); Doracus 'Alphabetum Francorum' (_0499, 2q2r); Otfrid (_0500, 2q2v); secret judges (_0501, 2q3r); 'Sequitur & aliud' (_0502, 2q3v); Hichi (_0502, 2q3v); Pharamund (_0503, 2q4r); Normanni after Bede (_0503, 2q4r); Latin numeral letters (_0504, 2q4v); numeral-letter cipher (_0504, 2q4v); Latin transposition (_0505, 2q5r); Theban (_0506, 2q5v); alchemist (_0506, 2q5v); Tironian alphabet (_0508, 2q6v); Iaimiel (_0509, 2r1r); Trithemius's own (_0509, 2r1r); then number tables (2r2r-2r4v) and the close (2r5r-2r5v). Book V supplies the tabula recta (2o2r) and the ancient numeral tables (2p3r-2p4v).

GOLDEN DAWN CIPHER = the alchemist's alphabet of 2q5v. Trithemius does NOT present it as his own: he says he 'found another alphabet lately made up by a certain alchemist' ('Repperi & aliud cuiusdam alchimistae confictum noviter alphabetum'), and goes on to disparage alchemy. The research file assumed 'Trithemius's 24-letter alphabet, a-z without j and v and with w last'; as printed in 1518 the order is a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r s t v x y z w - v is present (for u/v), u and j are absent, w last. The 1561 French prints u and ends with '&' instead of w, and re-cuts k, q, u, x, y and z differently (see the 1561 plate). Which cut the manuscript's writer followed cannot be settled from folio 13 at 453 px: the Küntz facsimile (1996) or the original is needed for x, y, z and u.

Trithemius's own alphabet: the only table he explicitly calls his own is the second on 2r1r ('nostrum subiecimus istud'). On 2q3r he also speaks of 'praescriptis novis inventis meis' (my new inventions written above), without saying which tables he means. The numeral-letter cipher (2q4v) and the transposition alphabet (2q5r) are presented as methods he constructs ('Iam nunc alphabetum ex his ordinemus'; 'Subiiciamus & aliud quod magis tutum iudicamus').

ATTRIBUTIONS ARE TRITHEMIUS'S: Wastbald, Doracus, Hichus, Pharamund (all via 'Hunibald'), Otfrid/Charlemagne, the Saxon judges, Bede's Normanni, Iaimiel king of the 'Articori', Honorius of Thebes (via Petrus de Apono), Cicero/Cyprian (Tironian notes). Report them as his ascriptions. Of the Doracus table he himself writes 'aliud ficticium alphabetum in codice Hunibaldi repertum', and of Hunibald's account 'sin autem fictio cuiuspiam est, neque nobis officiet' (both read on 2q2r in the LoC and Wellcome images; translation of 'ficticium' left to the editor).

checked.method: All 38 crops and all 32 page views in this folder were viewed (zoomed where labels are small). Each 1518 crop was re-cut at its stated geometry from a freshly downloaded master and compared: RMSE 0 against the JP2 masters (Wellcome _0496, _0500, _0504, _0508; LoC 0494), about 0.007 (Wellcome) and 0.015 (LoC) against the IIIF JPEG derivatives of the other pages, against 0.27 for a deliberately wrong page. The 1561 crop matched polygraphieetvni00trit_0412.jp2 at RMSE 0. Every page view matched its stated master. archive.org n-indices were checked against each item's scandata (Wellcome b33552137: 526 leaves, leaves 0 and 525 not in access formats, so nK = file K+1; BPL: same); loc.gov sequence numbers and image sizes against the item JSON; Wellcome image sizes against the JP2/IIIF files. Rights were re-read from archive.org metadata (b33552137, polygraphieetvni00trit), the loc.gov item JSON (32017914) and the Commons file-page wikitext. Crop edges were tested for black and red ink, and every flagged edge was inspected.
confirmed: Every 1518 crop shows the named table complete, on the leaf named: 2o2r 'Recta transpositionis tabula' (signed 'o ij'); Book V ends on 2p4v ('quintum quoque Polygraphiae librum terminamus. Anno dni M.D.VIII.'); Book VI begins on 2p5r ('LIBER POLYGRAPHIAE SEXTVS INITIVM SVMIT'); 2p6r carries 'In hoc libro sexto' and the heading 'DE ALPHABETO ET MODO SCRIBENDI Nortmannorum'; signatures 'q' (2q1r), 'q ij' (2q2r), 'q iij' (2q3r), 'q iiij' (2q4r) and 'r' (2r1r) are printed and agree with the file indices; red headings 'Alphabetum Francorum quod Doracus inuenit', 'HICHI FRANCORVM PRISCI VATIS alphabetum', 'Ex gramaticis Otfridi monachi wissenburgen.' are where stated.

Printed labels and their order are correct for all 1518 plates in both copies: recta key row (u, no v, no j, ʒ, w last; Wellcome foot row 'w a b c d a f', LoC 'w a b c d e f'); Normanni (A b c d e F g h / i-q / r s t v x y ʒ w, red numbers 1-24); Wastbald (Greek order, a b g d e ʒ / e th i k l m / n x o p r ſ / t y ph ch pſ ∞); Doracus (A b g d e [none] / f h i k l m / m n n o p ph / q r s ſ t th / v w pſ x y ʒ, 30 signs, 29 labels); Otfrid, judges (black sign, red label), 'Sequitur & aliud', Pharamund, Beda, Theban, alchemist, Iaimiel (a-w, 24); Hichi (30, m twice); Tironian (36, m and n twice); Trithemius's own (26, with ſch and th); numerals (44, a=1 ... q+sign=80000); numeral pairs (24); transposition (24).

The red labels that look like 'e' at the c-place and 'c' at the e-place (Theban, judges, Tironian) are the rotunda c and e of this face in alphabetical order: the same two shapes stand in the same places in every table and match the black c and e of the alchemist's table.
